title: UNLOAD-CHF Urea for Normalizing hyponatremia and reducing voLume Overload in Acute and Chronic Heart Failure
official: UNLOAD-CHF Urea for Normalizing hyponatremia and reducing voLume Overload in Acute and Chronic Heart Failure
summary: Main objective: To determine whether oral urea (15 g/day or 30 g/day), compared with placebo: Reduces the composite of Cardiovascular mortality and/or the need for hospital care due to heart failure at 90 days. And to determine whether oral urea (15 g/day or 30 g/day), compared with placebo achieves correction of hyponatremia (serum sodium ≥135 mmol/L) at Day 15 and Day 90.

interventions.name: Urea NM 15 g polvo para solución oral

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Heart failure, of any aetiology, regardless of LVEF, requiring hospitalisation or outpatient management with close monitoring in an advanced heart failure unit due to acute decompensation in a hypervolaemic situation, characterised by the presence of oedema, pleural effusion, pulmonary congestion or ascites, clinically demonstrated by chest X-ray or ultrasound.
2. Chronic treatment with furosemide, at least 80 mg orally or equivalent, regardless of the use of other diuretics
3. Plasma sodium < 135 mmol/L
4. Individuals over 18 years of age who agree to participate in the study by signing an informed consent form approved by the Ethics Committee.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Clinical instability at admission, defined by: Cardiogenic/distributive shock, with systolic blood pressure < 90 mmHg and mean arterial pressure < 65 mmHg.; Need for inotropes or ventricular assist devices and Need for orotracheal intubation.
2. Treatment with oral urea for 3 months prior to admission/randomisation.
3. Blood glucose > 250 mg/dL, or 180-250 mg/dL together with serum sodium of 133-135 mEq/L at the time of admission.
4. Participation in other clinical trials at the time of randomisation.
5. Any patient characteristic that may interfere with adherence to the study protocol or follow-up, such as lack of social support, substance abuse, or the inability of the patient/family member to understand the information and sign the study informed consent form (Appendix I. Information Sheet and Informed Consent Form).
6. Patients who will continue treatment with thiazides after inclusion in the study
7. Terminal illness/agony
8. Well-documented previous allergy and/or intolerance and/or contraindication to the use of urea
9. Renal disease with an estimated glomerular filtration rate < 30 ml/min/m2
10. Plasma urea ≥ 150 mg/dL.
11. NT-proBNP levels < 350 pg/mL.
12. History or situation of uraemic encephalopathy on admission
13. Chronic liver disease in Child-Pugh C liver cirrhosis.
